paragraphs.text: Tom Brown, a co-founder of Anthropic and the company's chief compute officer, plans to make a donation to Trump Accounts, the government-backed investment program for children, according to a person briefed on the matter who spoke to Bloomberg on November 20, 2026. Reuters reported the same plan the same day, citing a source familiar with the donation.
Neither report gave the size of the gift, and neither included a comment from Brown or from Anthropic.

Earlier on November 20, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in an interview with CNBC that one of the Anthropic founders would make a large gift to the program over the next few weeks and that the public would hear from the founders' families soon. Bessent did not name the donor or describe the amount. Bloomberg reported that its source confirmed Bessent's comments.

According to Reuters, Trump Accounts give US citizens born between 2025 and 2028 a government-funded investment account of $1,000. The stated aim of the program is to encourage investing and financial literacy from an early age. Bloomberg described the accounts as tax-deferred investment accounts available to every eligible child.
A day after a record-sized offering

The plan surfaced one day after Anthropic completed its initial public offering. Reuters reported that the company raised $93.5 billion on Thursday, November 19, after underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares.

Reuters described the donation as the latest sign of an effort by Anthropic to improve relations with the Trump administration. Chief executive Dario Amodei and the company have at times clashed with President Trump and senior officials over AI policy, the news agency reported. At a press conference on November 20, Trump said he has a lot of respect for Amodei, which Reuters described as a signal that the relationship is improving.

Brown has become a key liaison between Anthropic and the administration, according to Reuters. He appeared at a technology-focused G20 event hosted by the United States in August and at the launch of a government AI tool in September.

In NeuraFeed's reading, the timing matters as much as the gift. The offering turned the stakes of Anthropic's founders into publicly traded wealth, and a donation to a program that carries the president's name gives the company a visible way to show goodwill toward an administration it has disagreed with on AI rules. Until the amount is announced, the size of that signal is unknown. The details that follow, including the amount and whether other founders join, will show whether this is a single personal gift or the start of a broader pattern.
Bessent said the gift would come over the next few weeks, so the next step is a formal announcement from Brown or his family with the amount and any conditions attached.
